newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up on easier foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up on easier foreign investment.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Monday after the finance ministry raised the ceiling on single foreign fund investment in the island's equities to US$50 million from US$20 million from Monday, brokers said.
The benchmark index ended 34.19 points or 0.42 percent higher at 8,197.30, off an intraday high of 8,213.87.
Turnover was a heavy T$107.1 billion.

The market was also boosted by news that Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission said it had started accepting applications for the issue of warrants on more than 20 qualified locally listed firms from Monday, brokers said.
Tyre maker Cheng Shin Rubber rose T$2.3 to T$47.3 and bicycle maker Giant surged T$2.5 to T$47.4.
"China-concept shares rose on hopes that China will try to be bullish after taking back Hong Kong, but these firms are not supported by solid profit returns," Chen said.
Chen added that he doubted these shares can continue their strong performance in the future.
Electronics rose 2.29 percent on expected sound outlook, with computer giant Acer up T$3 to T$82.
But financials and constructions fell. For Tuesday, a 8,150-8,270 range was seen. -- James Peng (5080815)

Most warrant-eligible shares rose, with textile giant Hualon up T$1.3 to T$33.5. "Both news are positive, indicating the government's attitude to support the market," said HSBC James Capel analyst Alex Chen.
Recent consolidation had made many analysts predict a likely downtrend to test support at 7,800 points, but the government's bullish attitude may help reverse the trend, brokers said.

China-concept shares, or companies with invesmtment or investment plans in China, rose most on the back of gains in China-related shares in the Hong Kong stock market ahead of the British colony's handover on July 1, brokers said.
